name: marcella tomato sauce
instructions:
Marcella Hazan's famous three-ingredient tomato sauce. The simplest possible italian tomato sauce; canonical starting point for the family. From Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking.

See sibling recipes in the italian-tomato-sauces folder ([[sicilian-pesto-rosso]], [[vodka-sauce]], [[pasta-piperade]], [[marcella-eggplant-sauce]]) for other italian tomato-sauce shapes.

=== INGREDIENTS ===

- 28-oz can whole peeled tomatoes (San Marzano ideal — canned whole, not diced, not paste)
- 1 medium yellow onion, peeled and halved (NOT chopped — kept in halves)
- 5 tablespoons unsalted butter
- salt to taste
- pasta (short shapes preferred)

=== PROCEDURE ===

1. Combine tomatoes, butter, onion halves, and a pinch of salt in a saucepan.
2. Simmer uncovered on low for ~45 minutes, stirring occasionally and crushing the tomatoes with the back of a spoon as they soften.
3. Fish out and discard the onion halves before serving (they've done their aromatic job).
4. Toss with cooked pasta.
notes:
Marcella Hazan's 3-ingredient tomato sauce (Essentials of Classic Italian Cooking). Split out from the former italian-tomato-sauces.json (Variant A) into its own file.

=== WHY IT WORKS WITH ONLY THREE INGREDIENTS ===

Hazan's insight is that a whole peeled canned tomato + butter + onion, given enough time (~45 min uncovered), builds a sauce that reads more complex than the ingredient list suggests. Butter adds richness and rounds acidity in a way olive oil can't at this simplicity. The onion halves perfume the sauce without becoming a chunky component — that's why they go in whole and come out before serving. No garlic, no basil, no oregano, no chili — the restraint is the recipe.

=== DON'T CHOP THE ONION ===

The onion halves are meant to be discarded. Chopping the onion turns it into part of the sauce texture and changes the dish.

=== UNSALTED BUTTER, GENEROUS ===

Hazan calls for 5 tablespoons per 28-oz can. Don't cut it — the butter is doing structural work, not just flavor. Unsalted so you control the seasoning.

=== SAN MARZANO IF POSSIBLE ===

Whole peeled San Marzano tomatoes are what the recipe was tuned to. Other whole peeled canned tomatoes work; diced canned tomatoes read watery here.

=== SIBLING RECIPES (TOMATO PASTA SAUCE TAG) ===

- [[sicilian-pesto-rosso]]: raw blended sun-dried-tomato + almond pesto. Different technique entirely.
- [[vodka-sauce]]: tomato paste + cream cross-family outlier.
- [[pasta-piperade]]: blended vegetable-tomato base with optional savoriness additions.
- [[marcella-eggplant-sauce]]: fried eggplant folded into a garlic-tomato base. Also Marcella.

=== DIFFERENTIATION FROM THE RAGU FAMILY ===

This recipe and its siblings tagged 'tomato pasta sauce' are deliberately narrow — protein-free tomato sauces, whole-or-blended (never knife-diced into discrete chunks). For protein-forward, long-simmered, cutting-board-cut counterparts, see the ragu family: [[bolognese]], [[mushroom-eggplant-ragu]], [[fire-roasted-meatballs]].
